criteria.no: The item is silent about the directive, names the subject only, or plans a different approach.
criteria.unclear: The item refers to the directive's content in words too vague to tell whether it is planned.
criteria.yes: The item states it. The item says sanity-stack's claim has a timeout, that on expiry it reports the holder, and that dev-sanity then keeps the task active and retries.

addressed.instructions: Read `item.text` for this directive from `anchor.statement`: sanity-stack takes a timeout for the stack bead claim and on expiry returns the holder's identity, claim time and active task, and dev-sanity then keeps the sanity task active, asks the holder once, continues other sanity work and retries, with no refusal, no FAIL to the dev and no escalation to a person. Answer yes only when the item itself states that content. Answer no when the item is silent, mentions the subject without that content, or plans a different approach (for example it waits without limit, refuses the task, fails the dev or asks a person). Do not judge conflict.

criteria.no: The item plans none of the numbered cases; it may be silent about the directive.
criteria.unclear: The item may describe one of the numbered cases but its wording does not settle it.
criteria.yes: The item plans one of the numbered cases.

contradicted.instructions: `anchor.statement` says sanity-stack takes a timeout for the stack bead claim and on expiry returns the holder's identity, claim time and active task, and dev-sanity then keeps the sanity task active, asks the holder once, continues other sanity work and retries, with no refusal, no FAIL to the dev and no escalation to a person. Does `item.text` plan any of these: (1) waiting on the claim with no time limit; (2) refusing or closing the sanity task because the lock is busy; (3) sending the dev a FAIL because of the lock; (4) escalating to a person about the lock, for example messaging Rand, the user or a human operator? Silence is never a conflict. Also not a conflict: silence about the lock timeout; messaging the lock holder once; claiming and releasing the stack bead around a write. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.
criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.
